answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a single verifiable identity record, like an opal set in a fixed mount: creating a second identity means buying a second stake, so a Sybil flood gets expensive fast. Peers then weight endorsements by staked history rather than raw count, so one operator's many sock puppets echo each other without gaining influence. A velvet-smooth onboarding keeps honest newcomers cheap to admit, but the stake makes mass forgery cost more than any reward it could harvest.
